summary.intent: Run all 4 UAT tests for the phase-43 journal/sync feature against a full local stack using the existing headless login mode (`--dev-key`), rather than deferring tests that were assumed to require manual UI interaction.
summary.outcome: All 4 UAT tests were executed live on real infrastructure; 3 findings were discovered (filename cleartext leak, WriteParked unreachable at runtime, replay convergence failure for never-published IPNS records). F2 and F3 were fixed, regression-tested, and committed. F1 was deferred to an existing todo.

repo: `--dev-key` headless auth mode exists in the debug binary, paired with `/auth/test-login` (email `dev-key@cipherbox.local`, secret `e2e-test-secret-ci-only`) — designed for agent-driven UAT, documented in apps/desktop/CLAUDE.md.
Access token TTL is 15 minutes — live UAT sessions must complete within that window or restart the app for a fresh token.
`IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY` is optional in non-production: `jwt-issuer.service.ts:38` generates an ephemeral RS256 keypair when unset, so the API boots cleanly with only `NODE_ENV=test`.

This dev machine has both macFUSE and FUSE-T installed; pkg-config resolves `fuse` → macFUSE by default. The CI recipe avoids this by aliasing `fuse-t.pc → fuse.pc` (Version 2.9.9) — must replicate locally or the binary links the wrong lib and the mount silently never materializes despite fuser logging 'confirmed'.
The desktop e2e harness (`tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/`) is fully scriptable: `run-all.sh`, `wait-for-mount.sh`, `test-conflict-detection.sh` all exist and work against the local docker stack.
`replay_for_vault` already skips `Failed` entries (lib.rs:898) — the park semantics are correct once entries actually reach `Failed` status.
The background upload in read_ops.rs calls `record_failure` exactly once per attempt with no retry loop — entries can only ever reach `retries=1`, never the `max_retries=5` threshold needed to park.
`replay_for_vault` never called `record_failure` on replay failure — it only logged 'will retry on next mount', meaning replay failures were invisible to the park mechanism.

Per-file IPNS records created during live first-publish include TEE enrollment (`encrypted_ipns_private_key = wrap_key(file_ipns_key, tee_key)` + `key_epoch`) — replay must replicate this or the TEE can't republish the record after 24h.

code.finding: replay_for_vault skips entries with status Failed — park semantics are correct, the gap was entries never reaching Failed
F2: Err arm on replay_upload_entry only logged 'will retry on next mount', never called record_failure — fixed to call journal.record_failure(entry, &e)
F2: Second Err arm (replay_mkdir_entry) had the same missing record_failure call — same fix applied

F3: replay_upload_entry called coordinator.resolve_sequence() which errors 'not found' for files whose per-file IPNS was never created — fixed to detect not-found and create-as-first-publish with TEE enrollment
record_failure called exactly once per upload attempt, no retry loop — this is why entries cap at retries=1 and WriteParked can never fire at runtime
WriteParked emission logic in sync.rs counts Failed entries — correct, but unreachable because entries never reach Failed status at runtime (F2)
publish_file_metadata handles live first-publish: sets is_first_publish=true, seq via next_file_publish_sequence(true,None), and TEE-enrolls the per-file IPNS key — replay must mirror this for F3 fix
Generates ephemeral RS256 keypair when IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY is unset in non-production — API boots without secrets

workflow: When a dev machine has conflicting FUSE implementations, create a pkg-config shim (`fuse.pc` aliased to the correct lib) in a local directory and prepend it to `PKG_CONFIG_PATH` before building — then verify with `pkg-config --libs fuse` before the cargo build.
After a `kill -9` or force-unmount leaves `~/CipherBox` in a wedged state, kill the stale `go-nfsv4` process and run `diskutil unmount force ~/CipherBox` before relaunching.
FUSE-T mounts surface as `smbfs` entries in the mount table — check for `fuse-t._smb._tcp.local` in `mount` output to confirm the mount materialized at the OS level, not just in fuser logs.
The `bopnd2ejn`-style background task IDs from the Bash tool don't survive between tool calls — use `/health` curl polls or `pgrep` to confirm background processes are still running.
zsh glob patterns in Bash tool scripts that find no matches abort the entire command (not just that step) — use `find` instead of globs when the files may not exist yet.

friction: macFUSE and FUSE-T both installed on the dev machine — pkg-config silently resolved to macFUSE (kext not loaded), causing the mount to never materialize even though fuser logged 'mount confirmed'. Required a rebuild after creating a pkg-config shim.
15-minute access token TTL caused a 401 mid-test after elapsed wall-clock time during the FUSE-T debugging phase — required a full app restart before each test phase.
apps/desktop/.env was permission-blocked — couldn't read it to verify env key values; had to infer from `.env.example` and inline env vars.
fuser logging 'FUSE mount confirmed' even when the OS-level mount never materialized was a misleading false positive that took significant debugging time to diagnose.
zsh glob abort in a Bash tool script (`*.json` matched nothing) caused the entire crash+API-restart sequence to abort, leaving the app running and requiring manual cleanup.
`nohup &` relaunches inside tool shells didn't survive tool call exit — processes died, leaving mounts in wedged states.
Sandbox hypothesis (mount syscall blocked by Bash sandbox) was a dead end — required a rebuild before discovering the real macFUSE/FUSE-T root cause.
FUSE-T SMB mount pre-populates the inode table on mount — files converged remotely by replay are invisible in the current session without a remount.
open_items: F1: `"filename"` stored in cleartext in `cb-journal/*.json` — violates ciphertext-only journal requirement; tracked in existing todo `2026-06-13-encrypt-share-itemname-at-rest`, deferred intentionally.
Windows/winfsp build path (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/fuse/windows/mod.rs`) updated with the F3 TEE params but can't be compiled on macOS — correctness relies on CI Windows build.
Pre-existing rustfmt drift in `cache.rs` (flagged during format check but predates this work) — not addressed.
Files that converge via replay are not visible in the current mount session's inode table — require a remount to surface; no in-session cache invalidation mechanism exists.

WriteParked tray notification has never been exercised at runtime (only via unit tests that call `record_failure` 5× directly) — should be validated end-to-end after F2 fix lands in a real multi-failure scenario.
